title: Embed player never renders: .auritus-root stays empty
description:
## Observed

On a clean production build (`next build` + the static `out/` export served
over HTTP), the embed boots, POSTs `/jobs`, and polls `GET /jobs/<hash>`
successfully — every response 200 — but the element it mounts,
`.auritus-root`, stays empty. No player controls ever appear. The only
thing the reader sees is the first-paint placeholder chrome.

Reproduced on two pages, both with `rootChildCount: 0` after polling for
20+ seconds:

- `/examples/basic` — content hash `31491bc9`. That job is `done` and
  returns a signed `audio_url`, so missing audio is **not** the cause.
- `/` — content hash `2caf28aa` (the new home page demo).

## Expected

`mountPlayer` renders the controls and a status line into `.auritus-root`.
`embed/src/player/index.ts` already implements `statusLabel()` and a
"Waiting for audio…" state, so even a `pending` job should render a
player rather than nothing.

## Impact

No page can play audio, including the shipped examples. This blocks the M7
gate: "PyPI publishing awaits proof of live examples and fallback paths."

## Ruling out

- Not missing audio — the Gettysburg job is `done` with a signed URL.
- Not a dev-server artifact — reproduced against a static production
  export, not just `next dev`.
- Not CORS or site-key scoping — the preflight returns 204 and the job
  calls all return 200 from `localhost`.

## Leads

- Under `next dev` the player was observed rendering and then vanishing.
  `site/components/AuritusEmbed.tsx` calls `mounted.remove()` in its
  effect cleanup, and `reactStrictMode: true` double-invokes effects in
  development. That may be a second, separate defect layered on this one.
- The Claude in-app browser pane blocks the cross-origin API call, so it
  is not a valid environment for reproducing this. Use Playwright or a
  normal browser.

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Embedded player renders
  Scenario: A page carrying the embed shows player controls
    Given a page with the Auritus embed and a registered site key
    When the embed boots and the job API responds
    Then the player controls are visible to the reader
    And a status line reflects the current job status
```
